/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import itertools
edge_types = [1,1,2]
alternative_types = [1,2,2]
x = [0.3,-1.7,2.4]

def means(types, states):
    values = [1.0]*3
    for i, edge_type in enumerate(types):
        message = (x[i]+1 if edge_type == 1 else 1-x[i]) if states[i] == 1 else 0
        values[(i+1)%3] = (message-1)**2
    return values
max_error = max(abs(a-b) for states in itertools.product([1,2], repeat=3) for a,b in zip(means(edge_types,states), means(alternative_types,states)))
print('Three-node directed cycle; each source has an active state and an inactive state.')
print('Active labels:', edge_types, 'Alternative labels:', alternative_types)
print('Largest transition-mean difference across all eight regimes:', max_error)
print('Related by identity:',edge_types == alternative_types)
print('Related by swapping nonzero labels:',[3-e for e in edge_types] == alternative_types)
print('f0, f1, f2 derivatives: 0, 1, -1; g derivative at absent message: -2.')
PY"

strengths: Conditional summary graphs provide a useful representation of source-state-dependent causal structure, avoiding explicit enumeration of K^N regime graphs under the proposed factorization.

Combining per-variable latent switching with amortized graph discovery is a well-motivated extension of ACD/NRI. Supporting observed, observation-dependent, and recurrent states gives the framework meaningful flexibility.

The empirical results are promising: nearly perfect recovery with fixed synthetic structures, improved summary-graph estimation, and GRN F1 of 0.347 versus 0.187 for the strongest reported baseline by this metric.

The appendices provide substantial architecture, training, and data-generation detail, together with a code link. The paper also appropriately distinguishes population identifiability from the unresolved consistency of its estimator.
weaknesses: The central edge-label identifiability result requires stronger assumptions. Corollary A.8 incorrectly treats the aggregation derivative as independent of states and receivers around Eq. (46). Consider f0=0, f1(x)=x+1, f2(x)=1−x, and the permitted permutation-invariant aggregator g(H)=(sum H−1)^2. With at most one active incoming edge, both nonzero types produce x², despite satisfying the derivative-separation and nonzero-aggregation-derivative conditions. On a three-node cycle with active/inactive source states, active-edge labels (1,1,2) and (1,2,2) therefore produce identical dynamics without being related by a global label permutation. This directly undermines Theorem 4.3 as stated and is the principal reason for my recommendation.

The unknown-number-of-states guarantee also has a proof gap. Theorem A.6, Eq. (36), applies Gaussian-mixture identifiability as though all U components were present at each conditioning value. Observation-determined states can yield zero mixture weights. An explicit coverage condition and an argument identifying components across conditioning regions are needed before concluding that U, and consequently K, is identifiable.

Appendix B.2 does not establish the claimed exact inference for the non-degenerate categorical state model in Eq. (14). Future observations generally inform s_t, so setting the variational distribution equal to p(s_t|x_t) does not recover the full posterior. Shared source states also couple outgoing messages, and nonlinear aggregation prevents the claimed general O(NK) exact marginalization. The approximation needs a correct derivation or an explicit restriction to genuinely deterministic states.

The comparisons insufficiently establish advantages over competing switching approaches. Synthetic comparisons primarily use methods assuming a fixed graph over time and evaluate aggregated summary graphs; direct comparative evaluation of conditional graphs and states is missing. R-PCMCI appears only in the GRN experiment, using default settings after reported tuning difficulties.

The practical evidence has limited breadth. GRN evaluation uses one simulated bifurcating network and longitudinal measurements of the same cells, which the paper acknowledges are unavailable in ordinary sequencing experiments. NBA evaluates forecasting conditional on ball features, lacks causal ground truth, and shows only a small improvement over ACD. These experiments do not yet convincingly validate the inferred causal structures in real applications.

Statistical reporting limits interpretation of the gains. Table 1 and the NBA results lack repeated-run uncertainty, and graph-threshold selection is insufficiently specified. The GRN AUROC difference between SDCI and Rhino is only 0.936 versus 0.933 despite their much larger F1 difference; threshold sensitivity and precision-recall evaluation would help establish whether this reflects better structure recovery.
